'''Dieter Enders''' (17 March 1946 – 29 June 2019) was a German [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]] who did work developing [[asymmetric synthesis]], in particular using modified [[proline]]s as [[chiral auxiliaries]].<br /> The most widely applied of his chiral auxiliaries are the complementary [[:Enders SAMP/RAMP hydrazone-alkylation reaction|SAMP and RAMP]] auxiliaries, which allow for [[Enders SAMP/RAMP hydrazone alkylation reaction|asymmetric alpha-alkylation of aldehydes and ketones]].<ref name="Enders1976">{{cite journal |last1=Enders |first1=D. |last2=Eichenauer |first2=H. |date=1976 |title=Asymmetric Synthesis of Aldehydes and Ketones |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=15 |issue=9 |pages=549–551}}</ref> In 1974 he obtained his doctorate from the [[University of Gießen]] studying under [[Dieter Seebach]] and followed this with a postdoc at [[Harvard University]] studying with [[Elias James Corey]].<ref name="List2019">{{cite journal |last=List |first=B. |date=2019 |title=Dieter Enders (1946–2019) |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |volume=58 |issue=34 |pages=11554–11555}}</ref> He then moved back to Gießen to obtain his [[Habilitation]] in 1979, whereupon he became a lecturer, soon obtaining Professorship in 1980 as Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[Bonn]]. In 1985 he moved to [[RWTH Aachen|Aachen]], where he was Full Professor of Organic Chemistry and Director. He was [[editor-in-chief]] of [[Synthesis (journal)|Synthesis]] and was on the advisory boards of many other journals including [[Letters in Organic Chemistry]] and [[Synlett|SynLett]].

<br />During his career he won many awards, including:

* 1993 [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft
* 1995 Yamada Award, Japan
* 2000 Max-Planck-Forschungspreis for Chemistry
* 2002 Emil-Fischer-Medaille of the GDCh
* 2014 [[Ryoji Noyori Prize]], Japan
